name: French Quarter (White Town)
tagline: Pastel colonial villas and bougainvillea grids
description: The postcard heart of Pondicherry, a tidy grid of mustard-yellow and pastel villas draped in bougainvillea near the sea. Heritage cafes, boutiques and the Sri Aurobindo Ashram sit within easy walking distance, giving days a calm, photogenic, distinctly French-Tamil rhythm.
bestFor: Slow travellers and creatives wanting beauty, walkability and cafe-based remote work

name: Tamil Quarter (Grand Bazaar)
tagline: Busy markets, temples and everyday India
description: Across the canal from White Town lies the livelier, more chaotic Tamil Town, centred on the Grand Bazaar. Colourful temples, cheap canteens, shops and everyday commerce fill the streets, offering an authentic, affordable and energetic contrast to the polished French Quarter next door.
bestFor: Budget nomads wanting local life, cheap food and genuine Tamil culture

name: Promenade (Goubert Avenue)
description: The seafront strip along Goubert Avenue and Rock Beach is Pondicherry's social spine, closing to traffic each evening for a relaxed, car-free promenade. Sea breezes, statues, snack stalls and cool ocean views make it the town's favourite gathering place at sunset and after dark.
bestFor: Those wanting sea views, evening walks and central proximity to everything

name: Auroville and the Outskirts
description: A short ride north, the experimental township of Auroville offers forests, gardens, communal spaces and a reflective, idealistic atmosphere. Nearby quieter beaches like Serenity and Paradise reward those seeking greenery, wellness and calm well away from the busy old-town streets and traffic.
bestFor: Wellness seekers and long-stay nomads wanting nature, quiet and community
